refutation_attempt: Searched the whole TARGET tree for callers of CheckForNaNs and getDebugDisplayStringProperty, checked each declaration's access specifier, looked for XNA IL equivalents and for a CNA rule making them public contract.
reason: All CheckForNaNs and nine debug-string members sit in private sections with no callers; XNA 4.0 has no CheckForNaNs and CLAUDE.md says the internal DebugDisplayString must not become public API. The only public one, Color's CNAEXT accessor, is used by the C API. Nothing observable can be wrong.

refutation_attempt: Looked for any caller, friend or test reaching CheckForNaNs, so that the NDEBUG-dependent throw (Vector2/3/4 always, Matrix and Quaternion only without NDEBUG) could be observed; grepped the whole TARGET tree outside modules/math.
reason: CheckForNaNs is private on all five types and has no caller anywhere in the tree, so the NDEBUG difference cannot be observed; XNA 4.0 shipped no such member, and it is an FNA debug hook carried over unwired. Same conclusion as CNA-BUG-042.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed Game::Exiting is EventHandler<EventArgs> as in XNA, then read ExitingEventArgs.hpp, CNAEXT usage on sibling CNA-only classes, the C API mapping's own finding and the XNA comparison record for the type.
reason: Typing of Game::Exiting is XNA-faithful, but the header still says ExitingEventArgs 'Provides data for the Game.Exiting event' while nothing constructs or delivers it (CNA's own C API mapping records this as a finding), and the type, absent from XNA 4.0, lacks the CNAEXT marker CLAUDE.md requires, unlike sibling CNA-only classes.

entry.title: ExitingEventArgs is documented as the data of Game.Exiting but nothing delivers it, and this non-XNA type carries no CNAEXT marker
entry.summary: The header says ExitingEventArgs provides data for Game.Exiting, yet Game::Exiting is typed with plain EventArgs, nothing constructs the type, and it is not tagged CNAEXT although XNA 4.0 has no such class.
entry.expected: A type that is not part of XNA 4.0 is tagged CNAEXT (CLAUDE.md rule), so a CNA_STRICT_XNA_API build flags it, and its Doxygen says what it is used for. XNA 4.0's Game.Exiting is EventHandler<EventArgs>.
entry.actual: ExitingEventArgs.hpp declares an empty class under the Microsoft::Xna::Framework namespace without CNAEXT and describes it as 'Provides data for the Game.Exiting event'. Game::Exiting and OnExiting use System::EventArgs, and nothing in CNA constructs or raises an ExitingEventArgs; CNA's C API coverage mapping records that as a finding. The only tests construct it for its own sake.

sources.note: Exiting event and OnExiting typed with System::EventArgs
exiting-event-arguments mapping: nothing constructs or delivers the type

entry.evidence: Read the header, Game.hpp/Game.cpp raising path, the CNAEXT definition and its use on sibling CNA-only classes, the C API mapping text and the XNA comparison record; nothing executed.

refutation_attempt: Traced Latch and ThrowLatched for a race reachable without breaking the header rule; checked the release/acquire pairing, the only Latch caller and the class Doxygen wording of the rule.
reason: The header states 'All of it must be called before any graphics thread starts (see IsLatched())'; Latch writes active before a release store and IsLatched acquires. ThrowLatched runs only after a call that already broke that rule, so its non-atomic read of active is reachable only by a documented misuse. The separate latch-timing doc error is published as CNA-BUG-215.

refutation_attempt: Read Sharp Runtime's PropertyDescriptor at 41b918c9 and XNA's internal FieldPropertyDescriptor, then searched CNA docs and headers for any promise of value-changed notification.
reason: Sharp Runtime documents that AddValueChanged/RemoveValueChanged are not declared because std::any has no identity; the XNA descriptors are internal and CNA's docs/framework-design.md names std::any as the CLR object mapping and places PropertyGrid UI out of scope. No CNA text promises the notification, and the absence is a compile-time one, not silent.

refutation_attempt: Checked how registration is triggered (inline variable in every converter header, call_once in Registration.cpp), which headers include it, who else uses TypeDescriptor, and what docs/framework-design.md tells users.
reason: Registration runs from an inline variable defined by each of the twelve converter headers, so any translation unit that includes one is ordered ahead of its own later statics; only a static-init-time lookup in a unit including no Design header is unordered, which docs/framework-design.md ties to including a Design header. Only design tests use TypeDescriptor.

refutation_attempt: Tried to show the design tests do not run in CI: checked the tests' content, cmake/UnitTests.cmake linking of cna_design into CnaTests, modules/CMakeLists.txt inclusion and the exact ctest invocation of general-tests-ci.yml.
reason: design is always added, cna_design is linked into CnaTests, and general-tests-ci.yml runs plain ctest unfiltered; 25 value-level tests cover all twelve converters incl. cs-CZ culture. What is missing is an executed XNA oracle, the same generic gap already published as CNA-VGAP-046.

refutation_attempt: Took the dismissal's own admission that XNA's Decompose is a different algorithm and read that IL, the XNA IL review note, CNA's Decompose, Quaternion::CreateFromRotationMatrix and MatrixTests' Decompose cases; worked mirrored and sheared inputs by hand. No published entry mentions Decompose.
reason: The epsilon mismatch itself is unobservable, but Decompose follows FNA's algorithm, not XNA 4.0's IL: no determinant handling, so a mirrored matrix gives positive scale plus a non-unit quaternion and true where XNA negates the largest scale, and shear returns true where XNA returns false. A CNA test pins the FNA result and misattributes it to XNA.
read: CLAUDE.md::Where FNA and XNA disagree, XNA wins

entry.title: Matrix::Decompose follows FNA's algorithm, not XNA 4.0's: mirrored matrices decompose to a non-unit rotation and sheared ones report success
entry.summary: Matrix::Decompose ignores the determinant: a mirrored matrix returns positive scales, a non-unit quaternion and true where XNA 4.0 negates the largest scale, and a sheared matrix returns true where XNA returns false.
entry.expected: XNA 4.0's Matrix.Decompose (read from the IL of the genuine Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly; not executed) takes each scale as the row length, orders the axes by scale, substitutes a canonical basis for axes shorter than 0.0001, and negates the largest axis's scale and row when the basis determinant is negative, so CreateScale(-1,1,1) gives scale (-1,1,1), identity rotation and true. It returns false with an identity rotation when the squared determinant error exceeds 0.0001, as for shear.
entry.actual: Matrix::Decompose derives each scale's sign from the product of the row's first four entries (always positive for an affine matrix), builds the rotation with CreateFromRotationMatrix from the row-normalised 3x3 and never checks the determinant; it returns false only when a scale is within FLT_EPSILON of zero (the file-local WithinEpsilon uses 2^-23 with <=, and its comment calls that 'typically identical' to MathHelper::MachineEpsilonFloat, which is 2^-24 compared with <). CreateScale(-1,1,1) yields scale (1,1,1), the non-unit quaternion (0,0,0,0.7071) and true, and a sheared matrix yields true with an arbitrary quaternion. MatrixTest.DecomposeReportsPositiveScaleForAMirroredAffineTransform pins the FNA result and attributes it to XNA's 'per-row sign heuristic', which the XNA IL does not contain. CNA's own glTF importer relies on the result: BuildTrack decomposes a node's local matrix to fill the components an animation does not drive, so a node authored with a negative scale loses its mirror there.

sources.note: rule that XNA wins where FNA and XNA disagree
BuildTrack decomposes the node's local matrix (result ignored)

entry.evidence: Read CNA's Decompose, Quaternion::CreateFromRotationMatrix, the Decompose tests, the glTF importer's use, the decompiled XNA C# and the raw IL of Matrix::Decompose plus the XNA IL review note; mirrored and sheared results derived by hand from the code, nothing executed.

refutation_attempt: Read CNA's ApplyChanges, CreateDevice and INTERNAL_CreateGraphicsDeviceInformation, then XNA's decompiled GraphicsDeviceManager.ApplyChanges and ChangeDevice, looking for an entry guard or an earlier dirty-flag clear that XNA has and CNA lacks.
reason: CNA re-enters exactly as XNA does: ApplyChanges proceeds while prefsChanged_ is set, the event is raised inside INTERNAL_CreateGraphicsDeviceInformation and the flag clears only afterwards. XNA's ApplyChanges tests device==null||isDeviceDirty, raises OnPreparingDeviceSettings inside ChangeDevice and sets isDeviceDirty=false only afterwards, with no guard (inDeviceTransition guards window events only).

refutation_attempt: Grepped every reader of GpuDrawParams::specularEnabled and the comments that describe it; read the EnvironmentMapEffect setter and fill, the DIRECTX9 and FNA3D draw paths, plan_dx9 and docs/directx9-renderer.md.
reason: The functional claim fails: the flag mirrors the non-black colour test and D3D9EffectDraw and Fna3dDraw both read it. But IGraphicsRenderer.hpp still says 'No renderer currently reads this field', D3D9ShaderDispatch.hpp and DirectX9Renderer.hpp call the specular variants unreachable, and docs/directx9-renderer.md lists them as blocked, all contradicting the code and plan_dx9's 2026-07-16 resolution.

entry.title: Comments and docs say GpuDrawParams::specularEnabled is read by no renderer and DIRECTX9's specular variants are blocked, but D3D9EffectDraw and Fna3dDraw read it
entry.summary: IGraphicsRenderer.hpp says no renderer reads GpuDrawParams::specularEnabled, and two DirectX9 headers and docs/directx9-renderer.md call the specular and per-pixel-lighting variants unreachable, although DIRECTX9 and FNA3D read the fields.
entry.expected: Comments and renderer documents describe the code: after plan_dx9's D9-81 resolution of 2026-07-16 the field is forwarded by EnvironmentMapEffect and used to pick the shader variant.
entry.actual: The GpuDrawParams::specularEnabled comment ends 'No renderer currently reads this field'; D3D9ShaderDispatch.hpp says the value 'is not forwarded through GpuDrawParams today'; DirectX9Renderer.hpp says only the eight non-specular EnvironmentMapEffect ShaderIndex values (and only the 12 non-pixel-lighting SkinnedEffect values) are reachable; docs/directx9-renderer.md lists the specular variants and PreferPerPixelLighting as blocked. D3D9EffectDraw.cpp passes params.specularEnabled to ComputeEnvironmentMapEffectShaderIndex (all 16 indices reachable) and params.preferPerPixelLighting to the skinned and basic index functions, and Fna3dDraw.cpp passes params.specularEnabled to StockShaderIndex::EnvironmentMap.

sources.note: What's not (yet): specular variants and PreferPerPixelLighting listed as blocked

entry.evidence: Read the comments, the readers of the field, the effect setter and fill, and the D9-81 record in plans/plan_dx9.md; nothing built or executed.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a user-visible cost of the texture route: read the shader, the per-frame palette upload and release, the RGBA32F support check, and searched docs for any statement about pushed-uniform limits or bone counts on SDL_GPU.
reason: The 72-bone palette is stored exactly in a 288x1 RGBA32F texture, uploaded in the frame's copy pass and released afterwards, so all 72 bones work; the only failure is a thrown error if a driver cannot sample RGBA32F, which Vulkan and Direct3D 12 require. No document promises otherwise, so no limitation reaches a game.

refutation_attempt: Re-traced the default route: GraphicsDevice() default parameters, GraphicsDeviceManager::applyToExistingRenderer, Reset and NormalizeAppliedPresentationFormats, and whether any later renderer re-creation re-reads a Depth24 request; then looked for a documentation statement of the refusal.
reason: Game's device is built with default parameters (depth None), Reset normalises the requested Depth24 through GetAppliedDepthStencilFormatEXT (0 for Direct2D) before UpdatePresentationFormatEXT, and the stored parameters then hold None, so no re-creation passes Depth24. Only a directly constructed GraphicsDevice reaches the constructor refusal, which docs/direct2d-renderer.md documents (fixed DepthFormat None).

refutation_attempt: Checked whether the null device is a supported input: the constructor and its docs, whether XNA exposes a public ModelMesh constructor, and the construction sites; also compared with the published null-adapter entry.
reason: The ModelMesh constructors are CNAEXT (XNA's is internal) and document graphicsDevice as 'A valid reference to the GraphicsDevice'; Draw dereferences it as that precondition implies, and the null test guarding Ensure3DSupported only serves the zero-primitive fixture. A crash on a violated documented precondition is not a contract breach.

refutation_attempt: Read both version checks and plan_gltf's GLTF-033 row, then tried to construct a valid glTF file whose minVersion or missing version CNA would mishandle, and searched docs for a promise to validate the asset block.
reason: Both loaders refuse any asset.version other than the exact string 2.0; glTF requires minVersion not greater than version, so a valid file never carries a minVersion CNA cannot satisfy. Accepting a file that lacks the required asset.version is leniency toward an invalid file, and no CNA document claims asset validation beyond the 2.0 check.

refutation_attempt: Traced a negative or huge BoneCount through the constructor's vector assign to see whether it is undefined behaviour or a silent failure, and read the header for any documented exception contract of the CNAEXT class.
reason: A negative BoneCount converts to a huge size_t, so assign throws std::length_error (a clean exception) before RecomputeTransforms could raise ArgumentException. AnimationPlayer is CNAEXT, its header documents no exception type for the constructor, and only size mismatches carry an ArgumentException promise, so nothing documented is broken.

refutation_attempt: Settled the open question from SDL_mixer's CMakeLists at the pinned commit, then looked for any CNA header, doc, test or XNA contract that promises or excludes MIDI, and for a Song route that would accept a .mid file.
reason: At SDL_mixer 3075d3ed SDLMIXER_MIDI and SDLMIXER_MIDI_TIMIDITY default ON (only FluidSynth is switched off), so a Timidity decoder is compiled in; whether it plays depends on host patch sets. No CNA text or XNA contract mentions MIDI. The libcna.com page saying MIDI is unavailable is the site's own claim, not a CNA defect.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether any Song route or document promises MIDI, whether the build really compiles Timidity, and whether the format lists CNA does offer are already covered by a published entry.
reason: No CNA Song route, media index or document names MIDI, XNA's Song has none, and the compiled-in Timidity decoder is unreferenced build weight, so nothing promised is broken. The related mismatch, formats offered that no configured mixer decodes (.opus, .aac, .wma), is a different defect already published as CNA-BUG-052.

refutation_attempt: Read the public header, the backend interface and the SDL3 implementation for a contract that promises a fallback, looked for a capability probe that would make the silent no-op a trap, and read the Android and gamepad documentation.
reason: StartLeftRight is CNAEXT (XNA has no counterpart) and its header states that on a device without dual-motor rumble the call is a silent no-op and points to GamePad::SetVibration for gamepad motors; IVibrateBackend repeats it and Sdl3Haptics::PlayLeftRight returns false without SDL_HAPTIC_LEFTRIGHT accordingly. docs/devices-android.md records the phone blending.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a documented snapshot or consistency promise on PowerInfo, for a combined accessor in SystemInfo, and for XNA or Windows Phone behaviour to compare; read the implementation and header.
reason: PowerInfo is a CNAEXT class of three independent static properties, each a fresh platform read; its header promises no snapshot and even warns a battery status should never be treated as absolute truth. Each returned value is a correct current reading, and no XNA contract exists for it.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed XNA hard-codes CompletedSynchronously false, then compared XNA's pending-operation machinery with CNA's Begin*/End* pair, read the header comment, the callback path, EndFind and EndJoin, and searched docs and published entries for the synchronous behaviour.
reason: The property value is XNA-faithful, but XNA completes operations on a dispatcher thread and queues the callback to the thread pool. CNA's action is created complete, the callback runs inline and End* does the work on the caller's thread (150 ms Find window, up to 5 s Join wait, native builds). The header says the class 'never completes synchronously'; no user document records this.

entry.title: NetworkSession's Begin/End pairs are synchronous: the result is complete and the callback has run when Begin returns, and End does the work on the caller's thread
entry.summary: Every NetworkSession Begin* returns an already-completed IAsyncResult (CompletedSynchronously still false) and runs its AsyncCallback inline; End* then blocks the caller: 150 ms for a native SystemLink Find, up to 5 s for a native Join.
entry.expected: XNA 4.0 (read from the decompiled Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net and its async dispatcher; not executed) registers each Begin* operation as pending: IsCompleted stays false until a dispatcher thread finishes it, the wait handle is signalled then, the AsyncCallback is queued to the thread pool, and End* returns the finished result.
entry.actual: NetworkSessionAction is constructed already complete (IsCompleted true, wait handle signalled) and every Begin* invokes the AsyncCallback inline on the calling thread before returning, while CompletedSynchronously stays false as in XNA and the header comment says the class 'never completes synchronously'. The work runs in End*, on the caller's thread: on native builds EndFind waits a fixed 150 ms discovery window for SystemLink and EndJoin pumps the session for up to 5 s until the host's welcome arrives. A game that polls IsCompleted each frame and calls End* when it turns true therefore blocks there; the deviation is recorded only in source comments.

sources.note: FindSessions and its 150 ms search window

entry.evidence: Read the CNA Begin*/End* code, the header, the discovery loop and the callback tests, and XNA's decompiled async result, dispatcher and BeginCreate; nothing executed.

refutation_attempt: Read the header contract and the implementation for a promise of skeleton-identity checking, and for stronger data (parent indices, bone names) that a documented check would be expected to compare.
reason: AttachPartEXT is CNAEXT and its Doxygen states the BoneCount comparison is 'the one cheap, always-available check' that 'cannot detect a same-count-but-different skeleton, so callers are still responsible' for attaching pieces from the same canonical skeleton; the code does exactly that and throws ArgumentException on a count mismatch. The limit is documented at the API.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a CNA-facing path where byte-unit indexing leaks: the StringBuilder overloads of SpriteBatch::DrawString and SpriteFont::MeasureString, any System::Text::Encoding use in CNA, and whether the deviation is declared and pinned upstream and CNA's docs state its UTF-8 string model.
reason: CNA's StringBuilder overloads convert through ToString and decode code points, and CNA uses Encoding only for PCM names. The byte unit is a sharp-runtime deviation declared in its CLAUDE.md (#2015) and pinned by its Decl2015 tests, and docs/spritefont-support.md states CNA's string is UTF-8. It is a sibling architectural decision, not a CNA defect.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the WhenAll/WhenAny shape in the sibling header, then searched every CNA module, tool, example and test for an include or use of System/Threading/Tasks that would expose it.
reason: The only System/Threading header CNA includes is EventWaitHandle; no CNA source includes the Tasks headers or uses Task, and XNA 4.0's API has no Task. The overload set is sharp-runtime's API and nothing in CNA reaches it.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the per-task std::async and single-threaded Emscripten refusal in the sibling header, then checked whether CNA uses tasks anywhere and what CNA's own Emscripten threading document and CMake option actually cover.
reason: The behaviour is sharp-runtime's Task implementation, which it documents in its own header; CNA includes no Tasks header. CNA_ENABLE_EMSCRIPTEN_THREADS and docs/web-emscripten-graphics-limitations.md concern System.Threading.Thread and GL proxying, not tasks, so no CNA path reaches the refusal.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the std::regex ECMAScript wrapper and no-timeout statements in the sibling header, then searched CNA modules and tools for any include or use of System/Text/RegularExpressions.
reason: Regex is sharp-runtime's component, self-documented as ECMAScript-grammar and uninterruptible; no CNA module, tool or example includes it (only tests use std::regex directly), and it is not in CNA's default component closure.

refutation_attempt: Verified the Ubuntu-only workflow and the five failing Xml.Linq tests in sharp-runtime, then checked whether CNA links or includes Xml.Linq and whether CNA's own Windows and web evidence gaps are already published.
reason: sharp-runtime's NEXT.md records the five failing Xml.Linq tests and components.yml runs only on Ubuntu, but CNA includes only XmlReader, XmlWriter and Xml.Serialization headers, never Xml.Linq. CNA's own missing Windows and browser execution evidence is published separately (CNA-VGAP-026, CNA-VGAP-043, CNA-PLAT-015).

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the four component test directories are empty upstream, then checked what CNA takes from the Storage component and whether CNA's own tests and published entries cover it.
reason: The four sharp-runtime modules hold only .gitkeep under tests, but CNA uses neither compression nor the random module, and takes from Storage only StoragePaths (Android root and the isolated-storage override), which StorageDeviceTests pins. Other CNA storage evidence gaps are published (CNA-VGAP-038, CNA-VGAP-008).

refutation_attempt: Confirmed easy-gl's plain assert tests and default EASYGL_BUILD_TESTS ON, then searched CNA's presets and every workflow for a Release or RelWithDebInfo build that both has an EasyGL identity and runs ctest over the embedded easy-gl tests.
reason: The upstream tests do use plain assert, but every CNA lane that runs them (the unfiltered general-tests-ci job and the tests presets) is Debug; the Release GL-identity X11 job builds and runs only named targets, and the release and macOS presets use STUB or SDL_RENDERER. So no CNA evidence rests on NDEBUG-disabled easy-gl tests.

refutation_attempt: Checked the easygl::Config definition, how CNA initialises easygl::Device, and CNA sources and docs for any use of, or reliance on, enable_debug_logging, validate_calls or call validation.
reason: CNA calls device.initialize(glProcAddressLoader) without a Config and never mentions the two fields anywhere in modules or docs, so their being unread is easy-gl's own unused-field issue with no CNA behaviour or promise attached.

refutation_attempt: Read easy-gl's ResourceRegistry loops, then read every CNA release_gl_handle_only and recreate_gl_resource body and their helpers (CreateResources, InitializeResources, compiled-effect recovery) for registry add or remove, object construction or destruction, and for who raises the game-visible reset.
reason: The upstream loops iterate the live vector, but CNA registers and unregisters only in constructors and destructors. The ten recreate bodies and their helpers only create or reset GL handles; the comments about unregistering concern a separate ES2 level table, compiled-effect recovery uses CNA's own list by index, and the game-visible reset is raised after the registry loop.

refutation_attempt: Read XNA's TextureProcessor colour-key code and CNA's ReadCnjColorKey and ApplyColorKey to see whether a ranged key is any part of the XNA contract, and checked the published entries for the neighbouring colour-key differences.
reason: XNA 4.0's TextureProcessor.ColorKey calls ReplaceColor(colorKey, Transparent) with one exact colour, so a single exact key matches its contract and a ranged key is not XNA behaviour. The differing replacement value (key RGB kept, alpha 0) is already published as CNA-GAP-066.
